note_tweet.text:
Apple's CEO Wants Siri to Become an AI Agent, Gurman Reports

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple CEO John Ternus is pushing software chief Craig Federighi to accelerate the company's AI roadmap and move beyond incremental improvements to Siri.

The report, published in Gurman's Power On newsletter on November 8, says Ternus raised the issue with Federighi during a closed-door meeting in recent weeks. Citing people familiar with the discussions, Gurman writes that Ternus is frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors. Federighi has long been associated with a more cautious approach to AI, including concerns about its privacy, security and broader societal implications. Ternus has separately described agentic AI capabilities as promising.

What Ternus reportedly wants is a more agentic Siri. Gurman writes that Apple wants Siri to pursue goals in the way competing systems do. He names OpenAI's Dots, Meta's Muse and Grok Bot as examples of AI agents that can track goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without users initiating every individual step.

Apple ultimately wants to move in this direction, Gurman reports, and he believes the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year. However, this is his assessment, not a confirmed product launch date.

Apple's iOS 27.3 developer beta already includes more extensive control over native applications, allowing Siri to perform tasks such as cropping images in Photos and organising Safari tabs.

On November 3, Apple opened a developer preview allowing third-party apps to integrate with Siri AI through App Intents. This would enable tasks such as booking reservations through OpenTable or ordering food through Grubhub. App Store submissions will open in spring 2027.

For iOS 28, iPadOS 28 and macOS 28, Gurman says Apple has adjusted its development cycles to give engineers more time for coding, exploration and feature development, and less time for integration. Typically, each stage is divided into two four-week efforts. For the first M1 milestone of iOS 28, engineers were given six weeks for coding, exploration and feature development, followed by two weeks for convergence.

Gurman expects iOS 28 to enter beta in June 2027, with a public release in September. He has not disclosed specific consumer-facing features.

Finally, Gurman writes that Mike Rockwell, vice president of Siri engineering, is still considering leaving his position or Apple altogether next year. Rockwell previously led development of the Vision Pro headset before taking responsibility for Siri AI. If he leaves, additional responsibilities could fall to Amar Subramanya, a former Google executive hired to strengthen Apple's AI efforts, and Sebastien Marineau, a senior deputy to Federighi.
